tweet_summary: Headlined 'Erika Kirk responds to Druski's new viral skit on Conservatives,' the post shows a collage with a screenshotted '@MrsErikaKirk' tweet ('if I did blackface as part of a skit, I'd be cancelled and called a racist') presented as her real reaction to Druski's parody.
why_note_decision: The screenshotted Erika Kirk response is fabricated. Multiple fact-checkers (Newsweek, Snopes, Primetimer, IBTimes) confirm Erika Kirk did not publicly respond to Druski's skit, the claimed cease-and-desist is false (Druski's rep denied it), and the circulating screenshots of her replying do not exist on her actual accounts. Presenting a fake tweet as a genuine public response from a named public figure is materially misleading, so a note is warranted. (The original note's specific 'last post March 21' detail is a verification aid; the load-bearing fact is that she did not post this response.)
judge_guidance: PASS only if the note states that the screenshotted Erika Kirk response/tweet is fake and that she did not publicly respond to Druski's skit (and/or that the related cease-and-desist claim was denied). It must NOT treat the quoted tweet as a real statement by her. A note that argues the merits of blackface/the skit instead of addressing the fabricated screenshot fails. Cite a fact-check (Newsweek / Snopes / Primetimer) or her actual account showing no such post.
reference_note: The screenshot of Erika Kirk's tweet is fake. She has not responded to Druski's skit, and her last X post was on March 21, 2026.    https://x.com/MrsErikaKirk    https://www.primetimer.com/news/did-druski-claim-erika-kirk-tried-to-sue-over-viral-skit-comedian-s-cease-and-desist-post-debunked

fact_check.claim_verdict: False/fabricated: Erika Kirk did not publicly respond to Druski's skit; the circulating response screenshots are fake and the cease-and-desist claim was denied by Druski's rep.
fact_check.notes: Druski posted the satirical 'How Conservative Women in America Act' skit (Mar 25). Multiple fact-checks confirm Kirk did not respond on any platform; the cease-and-desist claim (Zellie Imani's now-deleted post) was denied by Druski's representative. The screenshotted reply is fabricated.

importance.lens_rationale: 1.3M impressions on a fabricated quote attributed to a named public figure, fueling a racially charged culture-war pile-on. Correcting fake attributed statements has clear value for discourse integrity, though the topic itself is low-stakes.
